The bug is in the pending state u1, which judges the step after a fall by holding_box alone. A second scheduled fall can fire on exactly that step: falls occur 2-6 steps after a pickup, and a re-pickup on the step after a fall can coincide with the next due fall because the action applies before events. Concrete reachable schedule: pickup at t-3, drop at t-2, second pickup at t-1 (schedules fall 2 for t+1), first fall fires at t while carrying; at t+1 the agent picks the box up again and fall 2 fires, so that step has box_fell true and holding_box false. The agent complied with 'pick it up again on your very next move' for the fall at t, yet (u1, !holding_box) -> u2 pays -0.5 and locks the episode in the failure sink; the new fall is never tracked and u3/+1.0 becomes unreachable although the task is still satisfiable (re-pickup at t+2, then exit holding the box) - task-perfect play scores -0.7 on this schedule instead of +1.0. Note that box_fell on the step after a fall actually proves compliance: hands are empty after a fall, so the box can fall at t+1 only if it was picked up at t+1. Fix: the next-step compliance guard in u1 must be holding_box | box_fell - add (u1, box_fell) -> u1 ordered before (u1, !holding_box) -> u2; the reward value is secondary (0 or +0.2 both keep totals bounded and unfarmable), the essential correction is routing back to the pending state instead of the sink. Minor notes: (u1, at_exit & holding_box) is unreachable in practice (a pickup and an exit move cannot share a step) but harmless; with the added guard the u1 else becomes a no-op - keep it for totality and format consistency.

Guards use only environment predicates (at_exit, holding_box, box_fell) with & and !. Semantic fidelity: u0 is the clean state; box_fell moves to u1 (-0.2), and from u1 the very next step must show holding_box (equivalent to the pickup action, since the fall emptied the hands) to return to u0 (+0.2); otherwise the RM enters absorbing u2 (-0.5). This encodes 'pick it up again on your very next move' as the hard constraint the emphatic wording demands, and at_exit & holding_box -> u3 (+1.0) vs at_exit & !holding_box -> u2 (-0.5) encodes the exit condition. Coverage and ordering: within each state the guards are mutually exclusive or order-insensitive, and every (state, labeling) pair maps to a transition - u0/u2/u3 via explicit guards plus else self-loops, u1 because its four guards already partition all labelings (its else is vacuous but harmless). Reachability and compactness are fine: all four states are reachable (u1 via any fall, u2 via either failure mode, u3 via u0) and four states is minimal for two obligations plus success/failure sinks; the defensive transitions (u1, box_fell) -> u1 and (u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u3 are unreachable given environment causality (falls cannot repeat without an intervening pickup, and pickup cannot coincide with stepping onto the exit) but harmless. def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing

def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step

def holding_box(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"

def box_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step

def at_exit(env): return env.grid.get(env.agent_pos[0], env.agent_pos[1]) is not None and env.grid.get(env.agent_pos[0], env.agent_pos[1]).type == "goal"
